title: Edgecohort calibration playbook — onboarding + rollback triggers
content:
Purpose:

This is a working playbook for onboarding new model variants into Hosted/Dedicated serving with a focus on small "edge" cohorts (low-frequency but high-impact inputs). Goal: codify signal definitions, decision thresholds, and rollback triggers that are specifically tuned to edge cohorts so we avoid both false alarms and silent regressions.

Context / problem statement:
- Recent onboarding runs highlighted two failure modes: (1) aggregate leaderboard metrics look fine while a small cohort of business-critical prompts degraded noticeably, and (2) noisy human evals make it hard to tell whether deltas are real.
- We maintain global leaderboards, but they lack granularity for CV/NER/format-heavy prompts and legal/finance templates used by a handful of customers.
- Need an operationally simple set of rules engineers and PMs can apply during canary/cold-start rollouts.

Definitions (how we use terms in this doc):
- Edge cohort: any prompt cohort representing <0.5% of traffic but >5% of error-cost (quantified in ticket severity / revenue risk). Examples: statutory text extraction, bank routing prompts, long-form policy summarization.
- Calibration: tuning decision thresholds (win-rate, quality delta, rerank loss) to match desired false-positive/negative tradeoffs for edge cohorts.
- Strict-majority pass: >60% wins in pairwise human (or synthetic) comparisons across the cohort, with min sample size.
- Sample floor: minimum N per cohort for a signal to count (see table below).

Quick summary recommendation (TL;DR):
- Require cohort-specific checks in addition to global leaderboards for any model variant serving >50 customers or touching regulated templates.
- Use a three-signal rule for edge cohorts: automated metric improvement OR strict-majority human wins OR no degradation beyond epsilon on calibrated quality metric. At least one must pass AND none may trigger a rollback condition.
- Set rollback on negative tail risk: if >10% of cohort queries produce catastrophic errors (hallucination of PII, invalid JSON) compared to baseline, immediate rollback.

Evaluation design details:
1) Cohort selection: engineering -> product nominate cohorts ahead of onboarding. Use: label, RLHF-flag, sample queries, expected outputs (gold/hard constraints).
2) Sampling strategy:
   - For cohorts with extremely low traffic (expected monthly <100 queries), augment with synthetic paraphrases and adversarial variants. Keep a flag for synthetic in eval logs.
   - For natural cohorts: random stratified sampling over time windows (day-of-week, peak/offpeak).
3) Metrics (automated):
   - QA-F1 / exact-match (for extraction tasks)
   - Schema-validate-rate (for structured outputs)
   - Toxicity-regression (for safety-sensitive cohorts)
   - KL-entropy-change on token distribution (to detect style drift)
   - Response-length-outliers (unexpected truncation/megahallucination)
4) Metrics (human pairwise):
   - Win/Loss/Tie counts using majority annotator vote (3 annotators default)
   - Severity label for each loss: minor / moderate / catastrophic
   - Annotator notes free-text (required for catastrophic)

Sample floors and statistical heuristic (practical):
- If cohort size >= 250 natural examples: require 50 human pairwise comparisons OR 250 automated examples for statistical confidence.
- If cohort size between 50 and 250: require at least 30 human pairwise comparisons and synthetic augmentation to reach 100 evaluation points.
- If cohort < 50: require synthetic + focused manual QA and product sign-off.
- Rationale: edge cohorts are noisy; guard against false confidence from tiny n.

Leaderboards and derived win/loss table format (how we report):
- Produce two artifacts per run:
  1) Cohort-level leaderboard CSV: columns = cohort, metric, baseline_score, candidate_score, delta, p_value (if available), sample_n, note.
  2) Pairwise summary JSONL (for auditing): each line = "cohort | example_id | baseline_resp | candidate_resp | annotator_votes | severity | notes" (we'll store these in S3 for traceability).
- In Drive doc summary include a bite-sized paragraph for each cohort: "X wins of Y (winrate Z%), top failure mode = <short note>". Keep it terse so PMs can scan.

Decision rule matrix (operational):
- Pass if any of the following:
  * strict-majority human wins (>=60% wins, min 30 pairwise) AND no catastrophic loss >2%
  * automated metric delta improves by >=5% relative for extraction / schema-validate-rate and p_value < 0.1
  * quality regression <= epsilon (cohort-specific) AND product signoff
- Rollback immediate if:
  * catastrophic-error-rate in cohort increases by >10 percentage points vs baseline (e.g., previously 0.5% -> now 11%)
  * any single example in live production caused PII hallucination and matches cohort pattern (requires immediate triage)
  * sustained human loss >40% across cohort after 24 hours of live traffic (rolling window)

Canary and rollout suggestions:
- Canary stage: 1% traffic, route to canary pool only for customers with opt-in or low-SLA. Monitor cohort signals hourly for first 24h, then 6h windows for 72h.
- Shadow-run: where possible, run candidate in shadow against same prompts so baseline + candidate logs available for automatic diffing. Essential for non-deterministic tasks.
- Staged increase: 1% -> 5% -> 20% -> 100%, with gating at each step. Each gate requires all edge cohorts to pass the Decision rule.

Operational playbook for engineering on alert:
- If cohort alert fires (metric delta beyond threshold):
  1) Pause rollout (stop traffic ramp).
  2) Snapshot failing examples to private S3 bucket and tag with reason.
  3) Kick annotator task for 30 examples (prioritize catastrophic labels).
  4) If PII or policy issues appear, escalate to safety + legal.
  5) If root cause is a prompt-template mismatch, attempt prompt shim in routing layer before rollback.

Practical heuristics and tricks we've found useful (notes):
- Use token-level diffing to find systematic truncation (e.g., candidate consistently drops last sentence on long prompts).
- Create a "canary prompt set" that includes 10 high-value edge examples for every release; automate a daily smoke test against them.
- Tag synthetic examples in logs so product/CS know which failures are synthetic-only.
- Where human eval budget is constrained, prioritize annotators who've seen the cohort (familiarity reduces noise).

Example cohort summaries (mock outputs for reporting):
- statutory-extractors: 45/60 wins (75%), automated EM +6.2%, no catastrophic events. Recommendation: proceed to 20% ramp with monitoring.
- bank-routing-long: 12/40 wins (30%), synthetic pass rate low, 3 catastrophic mismatches in sample. Recommendation: rollback; investigate tokenization / numeric parsing.
- policy-summarize-ES: 18/30 wins (60%), but KL-entropy-change +0.12 (style drift). Recommendation: hold, flag for product review on acceptable style shift.

Open questions / items for leadership decision:
- What absolute tolerances do legal/security teams require for PII risk in edge cohorts? (I suspect 0.0% but some small business risk tolerances exist).
- Annotation SLA and budget: can we standardize 48h turnaround for edge cohort manual checks?
- Do we want a distinct on-call list for edge cohort regressions (recommended yes for high-risk verticals)?

Next steps / action items (owners):
- Ethan: wire up the cohort-level CSV exporter into the onboarding pipeline (JIRA-MLONB-482) — due 2028-02-20.
- Priya: finalize canary prompt sets for fiscal verticals and add to Confluence page — due 2028-02-18.
- Samir: add automatic KL-entropy delta metric into the leaderboards and dashboard — due 2028-02-22.
- Rina: draft a short runbook for SRE on the rollback flow and paging — due 2028-02-17.

Appendix A — quick checklist for PMs before approving onboard:
- [ ] All nominated edge cohorts listed and owner assigned
- [ ] Sample floor met or synthetic augmentation noted
- [ ] Human pairwise required where indicated and budget assigned
- [ ] Canary routing configured and low-SLA opt-ins identified
- [ ] Linked failures pushed to triage board if present

Appendix B — short rationale for strict-majority threshold (notes to self):
- 60% win threshold chosen because with 3 annotators, it maps well to 2/3 majority while giving a buffer for ties/noisy votes; paired with sample floor reduces type I errors.
- We may revisit to a Bayesian decision rule later but keep simple for operational clarity now.

Notes / scratch (rough):
- Product asked for faster signoff cadence for Dedicated customers; consider a "fast-track" with higher sample floor but fewer human votes (2 annotators) for customer-paid fast-rollout. Need legal OK.
- Slack threads: #applied-ml on 2028-02-10 has early commentary and a few edge examples.

End of playbook (working).

-- Rina
